note.note:
Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes): 
  - Acute lower central abdominal/pelvic pain for a few days, progressive and severe (patient rates ~8/10).  
  - Associated nausea (no vomiting), light vaginal bleeding/spotting and small vaginal discharge.  
  - Recent constipation last week that has since improved.  
  - No chronic diseases documented.  
  - Conflict noted: assessment template requests Indigenous older-adult review (55+), but patient is 23 years old per transcript.

- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):  Not recorded.

- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines: 
  - Contraceptive implant: Implanon (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  - No other regular medications reported.  
  - Allergy: amoxicillin (allergy documented).

- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):  Not recorded.

- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks: 
  - Sexually active; reports recent intercourse (patient gave differing timings: "4 days ago" and earlier confusion).  
  - Last menstrual period approximately 2–3 weeks ago; periods described as irregular since Implanon insertion.  
  - Pregnancy test performed ~1 month ago (result not documented). Doctor requested pregnancy test today.  
  - No prior pregnancies.  
  - Contraception: Implanon inserted ~1 year ago.

- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use: 
  - Occupation: school teacher.  
  - Lives with husband and his family.  
  - Smoking/alcohol: patient answered "I don't know" when asked about smoking/drinking (unclear).  
  - Denies illicit drug use.  
  - No other lifestyle details recorded.

- Hearing and vision concerns:  Not recorded.

- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm):  Not recorded.

- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors: 
  - Lives with husband and his husband's family.  
  - No other social determinants or stresses documented.

Examination

- Vital signs: BP, pulse rate and rhythm:  Not recorded.

- Anthropometry: height, weight, BMI, waist circumference if indicated:  Not recorded.

- Oral health: gums, teeth, dentures if relevant:  Not recorded.

- Ear exam including otoscopy:  Not recorded.

- Eye exam: visual acuity, pupil response, fundus if indicated:  Not recorded.

- Urinalysis: dipstick for protein, glucose, ketones, blood:  Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Blood tests: fasting glucose and lipids preferred; HbA1c if diabetes present/suspected:  Not recorded.

- Renal function and liver function tests if clinically indicated:  Not recorded.

- ECG if cardiac risk factors present or baseline:  Not recorded.

- Cervical screening if eligible and due:  Not recorded.

- Mammography if eligible and not up to date:  Not recorded.

- Faecal occult blood test if due:  Not recorded.

- Bone density (DEXA) if osteoporosis risk present:  Not recorded.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Summary of key clinical findings, reasoning, and impressions from transcript and DDx:
  - Young, reproductive-age woman with a few days of progressively worsening, severe, constant lower midline abdominal/pelvic pain (8/10), associated nausea, light vaginal spotting and small discharge, and recent constipation that is now improved. Contraceptive implant in situ; amoxicillin allergy. No fever, vomiting, urinary symptoms, or hemodynamic instability reported. No physical exam or vital signs available; patient agreed to face-to-face examination.

- Relevant differentials from DDx that support/refine the clinical picture:
  - Adnexal/ovarian torsion — High concern (DDx): severe, constant pelvic pain with nausea fits torsion; surgical emergency to exclude.  
  - Ectopic pregnancy — Medium concern (DDx): pelvic pain with vaginal bleeding in sexually active woman; pregnancy test needed to exclude.  
  - Ruptured or hemorrhagic ovarian cyst — Medium concern (DDx): can cause acute severe pain and spotting.  
  - Pelvic inflammatory disease and gastrointestinal causes (including constipation/atypical appendicitis) — Lower likelihood given current data but remain considerations.

- Working diagnosis (supported by transcript and DDx justification):
  - Working problem list: acute lower abdominal/pelvic pain of unclear gynecological origin.  
  - Urgent gynecologic pathology to exclude, with adnexal/ovarian torsion considered a high-priority diagnosis to exclude; ectopic pregnancy and ruptured ovarian cyst are other leading possibilities.

- Considerations (additional plausible but uncertain options from DDx):
  - Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID).  
  - Constipation-related pain or atypical appendicitis.  
  - Implanon-related irregular bleeding (unlikely to explain severe pain).

- Immediate management and plan documented in transcript and supported by DDx:
  - Arrange urgent face-to-face clinical assessment with abdominal and pelvic examination (patient agreed; appointment to be arranged via support line).  
  - Perform pregnancy test today (requested by doctor). If positive — urgent review advised.  
  - Return/urgent review if pain markedly worsens, becomes intolerable, if vomiting and cannot keep fluids down, or if any signs of hemodynamic compromise.  
  - Recommended further investigations (consistent with DDx and to be performed after in-person assessment): urine/serum pregnancy test (if not already), pelvic examination, transvaginal pelvic ultrasound and beta-hCG quantification, and point-of-care or laboratory blood tests (e.g., FBC) as clinically indicated. Consider urgent gynecology referral if torsion or ectopic suspected.

- Conflict noted: transcript documents patient age 23; this note was generated under an Indigenous Health Assessment (Adults 55+) template — age mismatch.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  Not recorded.

- Patient health goals and priorities:  Not recorded.

- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA):  Not recorded.

- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports): 
  - Referral/arrangement for face-to-face clinic assessment documented.  
  - Recommend urgent gynecology/ED referral if pregnancy test positive or if clinical concern for torsion/rupture.

- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled: 
  - Patient advised to call support line to arrange face-to-face appointment; no specific appointment time recorded.  
  - Advised to return immediately if symptoms worsen or pregnancy test positive.

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral:  Not recorded.

- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management:  Not recorded (acute gynaecologic/surgical referral recommended if indicated).

- Dental referral if oral health issues identified:  Not recorded.

- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening:  Not recorded.

- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected:  Not recorded.

- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health:  Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Ovarian/adnexal torsion — High likelihood. Young woman with acute, severe, constant lower abdominal pain and nausea; surgical emergency to exclude.  
- Ectopic pregnancy — Medium likelihood. Spotting and pelvic pain in sexually active woman; pregnancy test required to exclude.  
- Ruptured or hemorrhagic ovarian cyst — Medium likelihood. Can present with acute severe pelvic pain and light vaginal bleeding/spotting.

Quality checks
- Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs, physical abdominal/pelvic examination findings, urine/serum pregnancy test result, pelvic ultrasound imaging, blood tests (FBC, beta-hCG), and immunisation review are not recorded. No documentation of STI risk assessment or cervical/ pelvic exam findings.  
- Internal conflicts or contradictions: transcript indicates patient age 23 while this template is for adults 55+ (conflict noted). Patient gave unclear responses regarding timing of intercourse and smoking/drinking (conflict/uncertain information).  
- Transcript quality notes: some portions of dialogue unclear or incomplete (patient name omitted, occasional unclear timing statements about intercourse and last period). Pregnancy test performed ~1 month ago but result not documented.
